name: Kaya Toast

instructions.primary_message: Stir the coconut cream. Remove the crusts from the white sandwich bread, then lightly toast it. Slice the cold salted butter into 1/8-inch thick slabs.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (14 ½ oz) can coconut cream, such as Aroy-D
2 slices white sandwich bread
4 tbsp cold salted butter

instructions.primary_message: In a medium bowl, whisk eggs. Strain eggs through a fine-mesh sieve into a large metal heat-proof bowl, and whisk in 1 cup 3 tablespoons granulated sugar until well incorporated.

Set the bowl over a pot of simmering water; cook, and, using a whisk or flexible spatula, stir gently and constantly, until the mixture reaches 176ºF (80ºC) and begins to set and resemble a thick pancake batter, 12 to 18 minutes.

Stir in coconut milk and continue to cook, stirring gently, until the mixture reaches at least 176ºF (80°C), 10 to 12 minutes longer. Remove from heat and stir occasionally to prevent kaya from overcooking.

In a small saucepan set over low heat, sprinkle remaining 1/4 cup plus 2 teaspoons sugar in an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until sugar has melted and is a dark amber color, about 6 minutes. Add coconut oil and, using a clean, dry whisk, stir continuously until smooth.

Pour coconut oil syrup into the kaya mixture and stir well to combine, making sure to quickly and constantly whisk to prevent the caramel from scrambling the eggs in the custard. Continue cooking kaya until it reaches 176ºF (80ºC). Remove kaya from heat and, using a fine-mesh sieve, strain cooked kaya into heat-proof jars, let cool, and refrigerate.

For the Kaya Toast: Using a butter knife or offset spatula, spread about 1 tablespoon of kaya over each slice of toast. Place 2 thin slabs of cold salted butter on one of the slices, and close the sandwich. Slice the toast sandwich lengthways and serve immediately with strong hot coffee or milk tea.

description: Layer kaya—a rich, velvety coconut jam with deep butterscotch notes—with thick slabs of butter for a sweet, tropical breakfast sandwich.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 soft boiled-eggs (optional, for serving); Hot coffee (optional, for serving)

Make-ahead and storage: The kaya can be refrigerated for about 2 weeks. We do not recommend freezing kaya jam. Kaya toast sandwiches should be eaten immediately.
author: Alia Ali
